summary: Source-anchored research for Credit expiry and History table. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: On organization Billing > Overview, Available Credits shows active and upcoming credits; expired credits appear in the History table below it. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
Available Credits shows usage progress for active credit pools and gray upcoming credits. Atlas draws credits from top to bottom in displayed order. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Subscription expiry makes Atlas use the configured payment method for remaining charges and revert subscription-paid support to Basic. Deployments must be terminated to stop future charges. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
Monthly Commitment unused credits can cover later overages during the subscription term; the documentation does not promise indefinite rollover. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
MongoDB for Startups gives 12 months to activate a code and 12 months after activation to use its credits. This is a program-specific rule. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-24)

For startup credits, Available Credits > Active Dates displays the expiry date. MongoDB considers extension requests individually and suggests contacting the program with three months remaining; codes cover future charges only. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-24)

On September 30, 2020, a Reddit user alleged that MongoDB Atlas promo-code expiry dates changed from 2099 to earlier dates, including expired dates; the post described this as affecting existing redeemed codes. This single historical account does not establish current policy. (low confidence)

SaaSOffers recommends tracking activation date, expiry date, monthly burn and balance, plus calendar reminders 60 and 14 days before expiry. This is third-party operating advice, not a documented Atlas alert feature. (low confidence)
